G8902.definition: to go out for foraging , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G8903.definition:
1. a foraging, a foraging expedition, foray , (Xenophon Historicus): in plural, foraging parties , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. an elephant's trunk , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. = προ-νομία, (Lucian) (ML)

G8904.definition:
1. an opening  or introduction to  a thing; in Music, a prelude, overture , (Pindar); in poems and speeches, a proem, preface, preamble, introduction , Lat. exordium, (Pindar) 
2. metaphorically of any prelude  or beginning , φροίμιον χορεύσομαι (Aeschulus Tragicus); μηδέπω ' ν προοιμίοις only just beginning , (Aeschulus Tragicus); εἴ τι τοῦδε φρ. ματᾷ if any part of this presage  be vain, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. generally, a hymn , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8906.definition:
reckless haste, vehemence, rashness, indiscretion , (Demosthenes Orator), etc. 
from προπετής (ML)

G8907.definition:
1. to fall  or throw oneself forward , as in rowing, προπεσόντες ἔρεσσον, like Lat. incumbere remis, (Odyssey by Homer):—;of suppliants, to fall prostrate , (Euripides) 
2. to rush forward, rush headlong , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. to move forwards, advance before  the rest, (Polybius Historicus): to project , (Polybius Historicus) 
4. προπίτνω poetry for προπίπτω 
5. to fall prostate , ἐς γᾶν (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8908.definition: in plural, like προπύλαια, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; in singular, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8909.definition: a going up, ascent , κλίμακος προσαμβάσεις ascent by means of  ladders, i. e. scaling  ladders, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. (Euripides); τειχέων πρ. a place where  they may be approached , (Euripides); δωμάτων πρ. i. e. the steps leading  to the house, (Euripides) (ML)

G8911.definition:
1. to strike  or dash against , τί τινι (Iliad by Homer); ἀψῖδα πέτρῳ πρ. letting  it dash against , (Euripides); τὸν πρὶν ὄλβον ἕρματι πρ. to wreck  his happiness on a rock, (Aeschulus Tragicus); πρ. θηρία τινί to set  them on  him, (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. δόρυ τινί (Euripides):—;without any notion of violence, to put to, apply , μαλακὰν χέρα πρ. [ ἕλκει] of a surgeon, (Pindar); πρ. παρειὰν παρηίδι (Euripides); ὄμματα τέκνοις (Euripides) 
2. to assign to, procure for , κέρδος τινί (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. Λακεδαιμονίοις Ὀλυμπιάδα to give  them the honour of  an Olympic victory, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. κακὸν τῇ πόλει (Aeschulus Tragicus); εὔκλειαν σαυτῇ (Sophocles Tragicus); πρ. δεῖμά τινι, Lat. incutere timorem alicui, (Euripides) 
3. with accusative of the object struck, ἀρούρας προσβάλλειν, of the Sun, to strike  the earth with  his rays, (Homer); of smells, βροτοῦ [ ὀσμὴ] με προσέβαλε (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. metaphorically to attend to  a thing or to add , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
5. μή μ᾽ ἀνάγκῃ προσβάλῃς τάδ᾽ εἰκαθεῖν do  not drive  me by force to give way, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. intransitive to strike against, to make an attack  or assault upon , τινί (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; πρὸς τὸ τεῖχος (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to attack, charge , (Herdotus Historicus); προσβαλὼν αἱρεῖ τὴν πόλιν by assault , (Xenophon Historicus) 
7. to put in  with a ship, ἐς τὸν λιμένα (Thucydides); πρὸς Τάραντα (Thucydides); with dative, Σικελίᾳ (Thucydides) 
8. Mid. to throw oneself upon, attack , τινα (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8916.definition: to look at, behold , (Mimnermus Lyricus), etc.; compare aorist2  προσεῖδον:—;so in Mid., προσορωμένα (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8917.definition:
1. to speak to  one, to address, accost , (Homer), etc.; πρ. ὀνόματί τινα (Demosthenes Orator):—;with double accusative, τί προσείπω ς᾽ ἔπο; (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to address as  so and so, πρ. τινὰ ὡς ἀλλότριον (Plato Philosophus); πρ. τινὰ χαίρειν to bid  him greeting , (Euripides) 
3. to call  so and so, to name , τί νιν προσείπ; (Aeschulus Tragicus); τοῦτο γάρ ς᾽ ἔχω μόνον προσειπεῖν (Sophocles Tragicus); ὅν μοι προσεῖπας πόσιν whom thou didst name  my husband, (Euripides) (ML)

G8920.definition: over and above, besides , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8922.definition:
1. soft, gentle, kindly , (Pindar); προσηνές τι λέγειν (Thucydides) 
2. with dative, λύχνῳ προσηνές, i. e. suitable  for burning, (Herdotus Historicus) (For derivation, see. ἀπηνής).  
3. adverb -νῶς, (Theophrastus Philosophus) (ML)

G8924.definition:
1. a putting to, application  of ladders to a wall, (Thucydides); of the cupping-glass, (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. an adding, addition , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8926.definition: to set on fire  or burn besides :—;Pass., σκεύη προσκεκαυμένα pots burnt at the fire , (Aristophanes Comicus): metaphorically, προσκαίεσθαί τινι to be in love with . . , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G8927.definition:
1. to leave besides as a legacy , ἀρχήν τινι (Thucydides) 
2. to lose besides , τὰ αὑτῶν (Thucydides) (ML)

G8929.definition:
1. to be placed  or laid by  or upon, to lie by  or upon , οὔατα προσέκειτο handles were upon  it, (Iliad by Homer); τῇ θύρᾳ προσκεῖσθαι to keep close to  the door, (Aristophanes Comicus); δοκοὶ τῷ τείχει προσκείμεναι lying near  the wall, (Thucydides):—; ὁ προσκείμενος ἵππος the inside  horse (turning a corner), (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. to lie beside, cling to , (Sophocles Tragicus): of a woman, to be given to wife , τινί (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. generally, to be involved in  or bound up with  good or evil, with dative, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. to be attached  or devoted to , τινί (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρ. τῷ λεγομένῳ to put faith in  a story, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. οἴνῳ to be addicted to  wine, (Herdotus Historicus); ἄγραις hunting, (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
5. to press upon, be urgent with  a person, with dative, (Herdotus Historicus); προσκείμενος with zeal , (Thucydides) 
6. in military sense, to press close  or hard, pursue closely , τινί (Thucydides); absolute to follow close , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ προσκείμενον the enemy , (Herdotus Historicus) 
7. with a thing for the subject, to fall to, belong to , τοῖσι θεῶν τιμὴ αὕτη προσκέαται (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. τινι δοῦλος (Euripides):—; to be laid upon  as a charge, to do something, with infinitive, (Herdotus Historicus) 
8. to be added  or attached to , (Sophocles Tragicus):—;absolute, ἡ χάρις προσκείσεται (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8931.definition:
1. to strike against , τινί (Plato Philosophus):absolute to stumble, fail , (Plutarch) 
2. to have a collision with  another, give offence , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. τινί (Plutarch) 
3. to take offence at, be angry with , τινί (Demosthenes Orator), etc.: —;absolute to take offence , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8932.definition:
1. Dep.: 
2. to reckon  or count in addition to , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. to impute , τί τινι (Plutarch) (ML)

G8935.definition:
1. a going  or coming to, an approach , ἡ πρ. μάλιστα ταύτῃ ἐγένετο the approach  was most feasible on this part, (Herdotus Historicus); ἀπείπατο τὴν πρ. rejected his advances , (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. μελάθρων approach to  the halls, (Euripides) 
2. an onset , πρόσοδοι τῆς μάχης onsets  or attacks , (Euripides) 
3. like πομπή II, a solemn procession  to a temple with singing and music, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. the coming forward  of a speaker in a public assembly , γράφεσθαι πρόσοδον to petition for a hearing , (Demosthenes Orator); πρ. ποιεῖσθαι πρὸς τὸν δῆμον (Aeschines Orator) 
5. income, rent , as opposite to principal, (Demosthenes Orator); often in plural, (Isaeus Orator) 
6. of the public revenue, φόρων πρόσοδος (Herdotus Historicus); χρημάτων πρ. (Thucydides); mostly in plural the returns, revenue , Lat. reditus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. (ML)

G8936.definition: intransitive to smell of, be redolent of , with genitive, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G8939.definition:
1. appearance, aspect, mien , (Pindar); periphrastic, σὴ πρ. thy presence , i. e. thyself , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. a seeing, beholding, sight, view , (Euripides) (ML)

G8940.definition:
1. to play  or sport with , τινί (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. absolute to sport, jest , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. with accusative, πρ. θεούς to sing to  the gods, ὕμνον πρ. τὸν Ἔρωτα sang  a hymn in praise of  Eros, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. to banter , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8941.definition: to sprinkle on  one, τινί τι (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G8943.definition: an ordinance, command , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; ἐκ προστάγματος (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8945.definition:
1. one who stands before, a front-rank-man , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a chief, leader  of a party, (Herdotus Historicus); ὁ πρ. τοῦ δήμου (Thucydides) 
3. generally, a president, ruler , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.; προστάται τῆς εἰρήνης its chief authors , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. one who stands before, a protector, guard, champion , πυλωμάτων (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
5. at Athens, of a citizen who took care of the  μέτοικοι, as the Rom. patronus  took care of his clientes;  προστάτην γράφεσθαί τινα to choose as one's patron , (Aristophanes Comicus); but, γράφεσθαι προστάτου to enter oneself by one's patron's name , attach oneself to a patron , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. προστάτης θεοῦ one who stands before  a god to entreat him, a suppliant , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8948.definition:
a deposit made by water , πρ. Νείλου, of the Delta of the Nile, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
from προσχώννυ_μι (ML)

G8949.definition:
1. to go to, approach , with dative, (Herdotus Historicus); absolute, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to come  or go over to, come in, join , τινί or πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus), attic; absolute, (Thucydides); also, πρ. ἐς ὁμολογίαν or ὁμολογίᾳ (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. to accede  to an opinion, (Herdotus Historicus); πρ. λόγοις τινός (Sophocles Tragicus): to make concessions , (Euripides) 
4. to approach , i. e. to agree with, be like , τινί or πρός τινα (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. to put faith in, believe , τινί (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8952.definition:
1. the foremost  or upper part of anything: a bust  or half-figure , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. the forepart  of a ship, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G8953.definition:
1. Dep.: 
2. to set up as a pretext  or excuse, allege by way of excuse, plead in excuse , with accusative, (Theognis Elegiacus), etc.; with infinitive to allege as an excuse that . . , (Demosthenes Orator):—;absolute to make excuses , (Thucydides):—;aor1 προφασισθῆναι in passive sense, to be used as a pretext , (Thucydides) 
3. to allege  (by way of accusation) that , (Plato Philosophus) 
from πρόφᾶσις (ML)

G8955.definition: a guard in front;  in plural outposts, videttes, piquets , (Xenophon Historicus); in singular, ἡ πρ. αὐτοῦ his advanced  guard, (Xenophon Historicus); διὰ προφυλακῆς with an advanced guard , (Thucydides) (ML)

G8956.definition:
an advanced guard : οἱ προφύλακες 
= αἱ προφυλακαί, (Thucydides) (ML)

G8957.definition: to keep guard before, to guard  a place or house, with accusative, (Homeric Hymns) (in the epic 2nd plural imperative προφύλαχθε, for προφυλάσσετε); (Xenophon Historicus); προφυλάσσειν ἐπί τινι to keep guard over  a person or place, (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute to be on guard, keep watch , ἡ προφυλάσσουσα (i.e. ναῦς); = προφυλακίς, (Herdotus Historicus): —;Mid. to guard oneself, to be on one's guard, take precautions , (Herdotus Historicus):—;with accusative to be on one's guard  or take precautions against , Lat. cavere, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G8958.definition:
1. at hand, ready , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of a drawn sword or knife, (Sophocles Tragicus); λίθοις καὶ . . ἀκοντίοις, ὡς ἕκαστός τι πρόχειρον εἶχε (Thucydides); ὃ προχειρότατον ἔχω εἰπεῖν (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. πρόχειρόν [ ἐστι] it is easy , with infinitive, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
3. of persons, ready  to do, with infinitive, (Sophocles Tragicus); with dative, πρ. τῇ φυγῇ ready for  flight, (Euripides) 
4. adverb -ρως, off-hand, readily , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G8960.definition:
1. lately, just now , Lat. nuper, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. the day before yesterday , οὐ χθές, ἀλλὰ πρ. (Thucydides); πρώην τε καὶ χθές till yesterday or the day before , i. e. till very lately , (Herdotus Historicus); so, χθές τε καὶ πρώην (Aristophanes Comicus); πρώην καὶ χθές (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G8962.definition:
the officer in command at the bow, the look-out man , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
 (ML)

G8967.definition:
1. first-born, firstling , (Iliad by Homer); φοῖνιξ πρ. first-created , (Euripides) 
2. of rank, πρ. οἶκοι high-born  houses, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. first-ordained , (Lucian) (ML)

G8969.gloss: to give a right of first-born
G8969.definition: to give a right of first-born

G8973.definition: to stomp; catch by a heel

G8975.definition:
1. mostly in plural feathers , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; in singular a feather , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. = πτέρυξ, a bird's wing , in plural wings , (Homer); Παλλάδος ὑπὸ πτεροῖς ὄντας, metaphorically from chickens under the hen's wings, (Aeschulus Tragicus): —; τῷ πτερὰ γίγνετο he got as it were wings , i. e. spirit, courage, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. the wings  of a bat (see. πτίλον II), (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. any winged creature , as the Sphinx, (Euripides); a beetle, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. like οἰωνός, Lat. avis, an augury, omen, (Pindar) 
6. anything like wings : as 
7. a ship's wings , i. e. oars  (compare πτερόω); ἐρετμά, τά τε πτερὰ νηυσὶ πέλονται (Odyssey by Homer); νηὸς πτερά (Hesiod):—; hence birds are said πτεροῖς ἐρέσσειν, (Euripides) 
8. ἀέθλων πτερά, i. e. the wings  of victory, which lift the Poet to heaven, (Pindar) 
9. a feathered arrow , (Euripides) 
10. τοῦ πώγωνος τὰ πτερά the points  of the beard, (Lucian) 
11. in Architecture, of the rows of columns along the sides  of Greek temples, see. ἄπτερος. (ML)

G8977.definition: attic -ττομαι, future ξομαι, Dep. to clap the wings  like a cock crowing, (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) (ML)

G8978.definition:
1. feathered , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. winged , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. πτερωτοί (i.e. ὄρνιθες); feathered fowl, birds , (Euripides) (ML)

G8979.definition:
1. to frighten, scare, alarm , Lat. terrere, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. intransitive to crouch  or cower down for fear  (compare πτώσσω), properly of animals, (Sophocles Tragicus); of men, (Pindar), attic; πτ. βωμὸν ὕπο (Euripides); also with accusative loci, πτ. βωμόν to flee cowering to  the altar, (Euripides) 
3. to crouch  like a wild beast ready to spring, (Euripides);—;so of men in ambush, ὑπὸ τεύχεσι πεπτηῶτες (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. with accusative rei, to crouch for fear of , ἀπειλάς (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G8985.definition:
1. white-rump , the name of a kind of antelope, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. the white-tailed eagle, the erne , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. (ML)

G8986.definition:
1. the hollow bottom  or stand of a cup , Lat. fundus, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. of the sea, the bottom, depth , (Hesiod), etc. 
3. the bottom  or foundation  of a thing, in plural, χθόνα ἐκ πυθμένων κραδαίνειν (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐκ π. ἔκλινε κλῇθρα (Sophocles Tragicus); δίκας π. the anvil-stand  on which is forged the sword of retribution, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. the bottom, stock, root of a tree , (Odyssey by Homer):—;metaphorically the stem  or stock  of a family, (Aeschulus Tragicus); σμικροῦ γένοιτ᾽ ἂν σπέρματος π. μέγας, i. e. great things might come from small, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
 (ML)

G8987.definition:
1. to make close, cover  or wrap up, enwrap , (Iliad by Homer); π. νῆα λίθοισι to surround  a ship with stones, so as to protect  it when laid up, (Hesiod):—; to cover thickly , of a youth's chin, (Odyssey by Homer); πυκ. στεφάνοις to cover thick  with crowns, (Euripides); so in Mid., στεφάνοις κεφαλὰς πυκασώμεθα [variant datesAnthology Palantina; also without στεφάνοις, to crown, deck with garlands , (Euripides):—;Pass., στέμμασι πυκασθείς (Herdotus Historicus); δάφνῃ πυκασθείς (Euripides); perfect participle πεπυκασμένος, thickly covered , ὄρος πεπυκασμένον a hill well-clothed  with wood, (Hesiod):—;Mid., πυκάζου cover thyself , (Euripides) 
2. metaphorically, Ἕκτορα ἄχος πύκασε φρένας threw a shadow over  his heart, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., νόον πεπυκασμένος, close, cautious  of mind, (Hesiod) 
3. to close, shut, shut up , ἐντὸς πυκάζειν σφέας αὐτούς to shut  themselves close up  within, (Odyssey by Homer); πύκαζε (i.e. τὸ δῶμα); shut  it close , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8988.definition: a gate-keeper, warder, porter  (see. πυλαωρός); (Aeschulus Tragicus); also as feminine, ἡ π. δωμάτων γυνή (Euripides):—;metaphorically, τοῖον πυλωρὸν φύλακα τροφῆς such a watchful  guardian of thy life, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G8989.definition:
a tablet of box-wood , (Lucian) 
from πυξίς (ML)

G8992.definition: mostly in plural pieces of wood , rubbed one against another to produce fire, (Homeric Hymns), etc. (ML)

G8993.definition: or -καυτος, burnt in fire , (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G8994.definition: wheat , (Homer); also in plural, (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G8998.definition:
1. to light up, kindle , πυρσεύσας σέλας Εὐβοίαν having lit up  Euboea with beacon-fires  σέλας combining with the notion of the Verb), (Euripides) 
2. to make signals by torches  or beacon-fires , (Xenophon Historicus): metaphorically, πυρσεύετε κραυγὴν ἀγῶνος give  a shout in signal  of battle, (Euripides):—;Pass., δόξα ὥσπερ ἀπὸ σκοπῆς πυρσεύεται (Plutarch): impersonal, πυρσεύεται fire-signals are made , (Lucian) (ML)

G8999.definition:
1. a firebrand, torch , (Iliad by Homer):—;in plural fires , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;metaphorically, πυρσὸς ὕμνων (Pindar); plural the fires of love , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
2. a beacon  or signal-fire, bale-fire , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. plural πύρσα, watch-fires , (Euripides) (ML)

G9000.definition:
1. fire-bearing , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of lightning, (Pindar):—; πυρφόροι ὀϊστοί arrows with combustibles tied to them , (Thucydides) 
2. in special senses, 
3. epithet of Zeus in reference to his lightnings, (Sophocles Tragicus); of Demeter, in reference to the torches used by her worshippers, (Euripides); of Artemis, (Sophocles Tragicus); but θεὸς πυρφόρος the fire-bearing  god, the god who produces plague  or fever , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. ὁ πυρφόρος, in the Lacedaemonian army, was the priest who kept the sacrificial fire , which was never allowed to go out, (Xenophon Historicus); hence proverbial of a total defeat, ἔδεε δὲ μηδὲ πυρφόρον περιγενέσθαι (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9002.definition: the beard , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;metaphorically, πώγων πυρός a beard  or tail  of fire, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9006.definition: to leave off work, to be remiss , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9007.definition:
1. to sprinkle, besprinkle , ῥάσσατε (i.e. δῶμα ὕδατι) (Odyssey by Homer); αἵματι βωμόν (Euripides):—;Pass., πύργοι αἵματι ἐρράδατ᾽ (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι δ᾽ ἐρράδαται τοῖχοι (Odyssey by Homer):—;of dust, ἵπποι ῥαίνοντο κονίηι (Iliad by Homer) 
2. metaphorically, ῥ. τινὰ ὕμνωι (Pindar) 
3. to sprinkle , with accusative of the thing sprinkled, ῥαίνειν ἐς τὰ βλέφαρα to sprinkle  (vinegar) in their eyes, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9012.definition:
1. stitched, patched , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. metaphorically strung together, continuous , of verses, (Pindar) 
3. worked with the needle : ῥαπτόν, οῦ, an embroidered carpet , (Xenophon Historicus); ῥαπτὴ σφαῖρα a stitched  ball, of divers colours, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
 (ML)

G9013.definition:
1. to sew  or stitch together, stich , (Iliad by Homer):—; Mid., ῥάπτεσθαι ὀχετὸν δερμάτων to make oneself  a pipe of leather, (Herdotus Historicus); ῥαψάμενος τουτί (i.e. τὸ προσκεφάλαιον) having got  it stitched , (Aristophanes Comicus); but also, to sew on  or to one , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Pass., ἐρράφθαι τὸ χεῖλος to have  one's lip sewed up , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. metaphorically to devise, contrive, plot , (Homer), etc.; proverbial, τὸ ὑπόδημα ἔρραψας μὲν σύ, ὑπεδήσατο δὲ Ἀρισταγόρης you made the shoe , but Aristagoras put it on, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9018.definition:
1. the lower part of the back, the chine , (Iliad by Homer): then, the spine  or backbone , ὑπὸ ῥάχιν παγῆναι to be impaled, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. anything ridged like the backbone, a mountain-ridge , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9022.definition:

G9217.definition: made of the wood of the tree  στύραξ, (Strabo Geographus) (ML)

G9219.definition:
1. a writing  or noting down , (Herdotus Historicus)

G9221.definition: set on fire with  or at once, burn up , Lat. comburere, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9261.definition: advice  or counsel given , (Herdotus Historicus); in plural counsels , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9326.definition:
1. a composition , of words and sentences, (Lucian) 
2. a conventional agreement, convention, compact , (Plato Philosophus); ἐκ συνθήκης, ex composito, by agreement , (Plato Philosophus); κατὰ συνθήκην conventionally , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. the article of a compact  or treaty , (Thucydides):—;mostly in plural the articles of agreement , and collectively, a contract, compact, covenant, treaty , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; συνθήκας ποιέεσθαί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); ἐκ τῶν συνθηκῶν according to the covenant , (Isocrates Orator); κατὰ τὰς ς. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9327.definition:
1. knowing along with  another, conscious , ὡς θεοὶ ξυνίστορες as the gods are witnesses , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc. 
2. with accusative (with the verbal construction), πολλὰ συνίστορα κακά conscious of  many evils, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9332.definition:
1. to make to live with , (Isocrates Orator); ς. τινὶ τὴν θυγατέρα to give  him one's daughter in marriage , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. to combine in one city, unite under a capital  or metropolis , ξ. πάντας (i.e. ἐς τὰς Ἀθήνας)) (Thucydides):—;Pass., ξυνοικισθείσης πόλεως the city having been regularly formed , opposite to κατὰ κώμας οἰκίζεσθαι, (Thucydides) 
3. to join in peopling  or colonising  a country, (Euripides) 
4. generally to unite, associate , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9335.definition:
1. that which is put together in order : 
2. a body  of troops, squadron, contingent , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. the constitution of a state , ς. πολιτείας a form  of constitution, (Isocrates Orator) 
4. an arrangement of musical notes , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. a regular collection of writings, a work, book, doctrine , (Plutarch) 
6. = σύνταξις II. 3, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9336.definition:
1. a putting together, arranging, arrangement, organisation, order , (Thucydides): rule , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. a systematic treatise , (Aristotle Philosopher): a narrative , (Polybius Historicus) 
3. grammatical construction, syntax , (Lucian) 
4. a body of troops , ἡ εἰς μυρίους ς. their contingent  towards 10, 000, (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. a covenant, contract , (Demosthenes Orator) 
6. an assigned impost, contribution , (Demosthenes Orator) 
7. a payment, allowance, pension , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9337.definition: to throw all together into confusion, to confound, disturb, trouble , Lat. conturbare, (Iliad by Homer), attic:—;Pass., αἰθὴρ πόντῳ ξυντετάρακται air is confounded with  sea, (Aeschulus Tragicus): to be thrown into confusion , of soldiers, (Thucydides); of social order, (Sophocles Tragicus); metaphorically of persons, to be confounded, greatly troubled, much distressed , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9344.definition: to weave together : metaphorically to frame with art, devise cunningly , (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ὥστε ταῦτα συνυφανθῆναι so that this web was woven , i. e. this business undertaken, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9348.definition:
1. a pipe : 
2. a musical pipe, a shepherd's pipe, Panspipe , (Iliad by Homer), attic 
3. anything like a pipe : 
4. a spear-case , = δορατοθήκη, (Iliad by Homer) 
5. the hole in the nave of a wheel , [variant datesTragica Adespota 
6. a duct  or channel  in the body, in plural the nostrils , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
 (ML)

G9349.definition:
1. to play the  σῦριγξ, to pipe , (Euripides); with accusative cognate, συρίζων ὑμεναίους (Euripides) 
2. to whistle, hiss , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;with accusative cognate, συρίζων φόνον hissing forth  murder, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. to hiss  an actor, Lat. explodere, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9351.definition: to sew  or stitch together, sew up , Lat. consuo, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9352.definition: one who lives in the same tent, a messmate , Lat. contubernalis, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9353.definition:
1. to shade quite over, throw a shade over, shade closely  or thickly , (Hesiod); γένυν ς., i. e.to get a beard, (Euripides): metaphorically, συσκηνῶσαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. intransitive to be thick-shaded , (Euripides) (ML)

G9354.definition: closely shaded, thickly shaded , (Xenophon Historicus); σύσκιόν τι a closely-shaded place , (Lucian) (ML)

G9355.definition: to grow quite dark : impersonal, συσκοτάζει it grows dark , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9356.definition:
1. to draw together, draw up, contract , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to draw together  by stitching, sew together , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. in Mid. to draw along with one , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9359.definition:
1. a putting together, composition , (Aristotle Philosopher); ς. προσώπου a studied expression  of countenance, of Pericles, (Plutarch) 
2. a bringing together, introduction, recommendation , (Polybius Historicus) 
3.  συνίσταμαι); a standing together, meeting : in hostile sense, close combat, conflict , (Herdotus Historicus); metaphorically, ς. γνώμης a conflict  of mind, intense anxiety, (Thucydides) 
4. a meeting, a knot of men , (Euripides); κατὰ ξυστάσεις γιγνόμενοι forming into knots , (Thucydides): a political union , (Demosthenes Orator) 
5. friendship  or alliance , (Polybius Historicus): a conspiracy , (Plutarch) 
6. construction, structure, constitution , (Plato Philosophus): absolute a political constitution , (Plato Philosophus) 
7. metaphorically of the mind, ς. φρενῶν contraction, sternness, sullenness , (Euripides) (ML)

G9361.definition:
anything twisted up together: a body of men, a crowd, concourse , (Polybius Historicus) 
from συστρέφω (ML)

G9364.definition: to be gangrened , ἐσφακέλισε τὸ ὀστέον (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9365.definition:
1. likely to make one stumble  or trip : metaphorically slippery, perilous, dangerous , Lat. lubricus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; σφαλερόν [ ἐστι], with infinitive, it is dangerous  to . ., (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
2.  σφάλλομαι); ready to fall, tottering, reeling, staggering , (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφ. σύμμαχοι (Demosthenes Orator) 
 (ML)

G9366.definition:
1. Lat. fall-o (the sigma being lost):—; to make to fall, throw down, overthrow , properly by tripping up, to trip up in wrestling , (Homer), etc.; σφ. ναῦς to throw  her on her beam-ends , (Plutarch); ἵππος σφ. τὸν ἀναβάτην throws  him, (Xenophon Historicus):—;Pass. to be tripped up , (Aristophanes Comicus); of a drunken man, σφαλλόμενος reeling, staggering , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. generally, to cause to fall, overthrow, defeat , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to be overthrown, to fall, fail, be undone, become helpless , (Herdotus Historicus), attic; τόδ᾽ ἐσφάλη this mishap took place , (Sophocles Tragicus); οὔ τι μὴ σφαλῶ γ᾽ ἐν σοί I shall  not fail  in thy business, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. to baffle, foil, balk, disappoint , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to err, go wrong, be mistaken , (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. the Pass. is also used with genitive rei, to be balked of  or foiled in  a thing, ἦ καὶ πατήρ τι σφάλλεται βουλευμάτω; (Aeschulus Tragicus); σφάλλεσθαι γάμου (Euripides); τῆς δόξης (Thucydides) (ML)

G9368.definition:
1. to sling, to use the sling , (Thucydides) 
2. to strike by slinging , (Babrius Fabularum Scriptor) 
3. to throw as from a sling :—;Pass., (Euripides) 
4. to move like a swing, to swing to and fro , (Euripides) 
from σφενδόνη (ML)

G9369.definition:
1. Lat. funda (the ς being lost), a sling , (Iliad by Homer): metaphorically, σφενδόνας ἀπ᾽ εὐμέτρου with well-measured throw, as from a sling , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. the hoop  of a ring in which the stone was set  as in a sling, especially the broader part round the stone , as in Lat. funda for pala annuli , (Euripides) 
3. the stone  or bullet of the sling , (Xenophon Historicus); τοιαύταις σφ., of hailstones, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9373.definition: to bind tight, bind fast , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9374.definition:
1. vehement, violent, excessive , (Thucydides), etc. 
2. of men, violent, impetuous , (Plato Philosophus): also strong, robust , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9375.definition:
1. a vertebra , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in plural the backbone, spine , or the neck , (Euripides) 
2. Lat. verticillus, the round weight attached to a spindle, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9376.definition:
1. a hammer , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. a beetle, mallet , for breaking clods of earth, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9379.definition:
1. properly to let loose : hence to slit, open , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. φλέβα to open  a vein, (Xenophon Historicus), etc.:—;of flowers, σχ. κάλυκας [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. to let fall, drop , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. to let go , σχάσας τὴν φροντίδα having let  the mind go, given  it play , (Aristophanes Comicus); σχ. τὰς μηχανάς to let off  the engines, (Plutarch) 
4. to check, stop, stay , Lat. inhibere, κώπαν σχάσον, i. e. cease rowing, (Pindar); σχάσον ὄμμα lower  thine eyes, (Euripides):—;Mid., σχασάμενος τὴν ἱππικήν having dropt  one's horsemanship, given up the turf, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9380.definition:
1. a raft, float  (such as was made off-hand , compare σχέδιος II), (Odyssey by Homer); generally, a boat, ship , (Euripides) 
2. a bridge of boats , of the bridge of Xerxes, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9382.definition:
1. a piece of wood cleft off, a lath, splinter , Lat. scindula, (Odyssey by Homer): in plural cleft wood, fire-wood , (Homer) 
2. an arrow , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
 (ML)

G9385.definition: a measured out line; a piece of measured out land

G9386.gloss: a piece of measured out land
G9386.definition: a fencing with ropes : in plural roping, rope-fences , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9387.definition:
1. a rush , Lat. juncus, scirpus, (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
2. a reed , used as an arrow  or javelin , (Batrachomyomachia) 
3. a place where rushes grow, a rushbed , (Odyssey by Homer) 
4. a rush-rope , and generally, a rope, cord , (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus) 
5. a fence  round a garden, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
6. a land-measure , = 2 Persian parasangs, = 60 stades, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9388.definition:
1. one who lives at ease , (Plutarch) 
2. as adjective leisurely, idle , βίος (Plutarch) (ML)

G9389.definition:
1. to make into a body, to consolidate, organise , (Polybius Historicus) 
2. to provide with bodily strength, to recruit , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9391.definition:
1. a heap , Lat. acervus, (Hesiod), etc. 
2. generally, a heap, quantity , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9394.definition:
1. a band, riband, fillet , especially a head-band , worn in sign of victory, (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
2. a strip  or tongue of land , (Plutarch), etc. (ML)

G9395.definition: fit for ordering  or arranging , especially in war, τ. ἀνήρ a tactician , (Xenophon Historicus); τακτικὸν ἡγεῖσθαί τι to think it a good piece of tactics , (Xenophon Historicus); οἱ τ. ἀριθμοί the regular battalions, (Xenophon Historicus): τὰ τακτικά the art of drawing up soldiers in array, tactics , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9397.definition:
suffering, wretched , Lat. miser, (Odyssey by Homer); ὦ τάλαιν᾽ ἐγώ (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὦ τάλαν (Sophocles Tragicus);—;with genitive causae, τάλαιν᾽ ἐγὼ τῆς ὕβρεως wretched that I am  for this insolence, (Aristophanes Comicus):—;in bad sense, τάλαν wretch!  (Odyssey by Homer)—;comparative τᾶλάντερος, η, ον: Sup. τᾶλάντατος, η, ον, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 τᾶλα_; doric also τᾶλᾶς: vocative τάλᾶν. (ML)

G9398.definition:
1. one who carves and distributes, a dispenser , (Iliad by Homer):—;of Zeus, as the dispenser  of all things to men, (Iliad by Homer); so Aeolus is τ. ἀνέμων (Odyssey by Homer):—;of kings or rulers, a controller, director , (Pindar); τ. κώμων master  of the revels, (Pindar); τ. Διός the priest  of Zeus, (Pindar): τ. Μοισᾶν, i. e. a poet, (Pindar); οἶκος τ. στεφάνων that hath store  of crowns, (Pindar); τῆς τε ἐπιθυμίας καὶ τῆς τύχης τ. controller  both of his desire and of fortune, (Thucydides); τ. τριαίνης, of Poseidon, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. in Prose, a controller  of payments, treasurer , (Herdotus Historicus); τ. τοῦ ἱροῦ the controller  of the sacred treasure in the citadel of Athens, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. at Rome, the quaestor , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9399.definition:
1. to be controller  of receipts and expenditure, to be treasurer, paymaster , (Aristophanes Comicus):—;with genitive, τ. τῆς Παράλου to be paymaster of  the Paralus, (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. at Rome, to be quaestor , (Plutarch) 
3. transitive to deal out, dispense , (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;Pass., τοὺς νόμους τεταμιεύμεθα we have  the laws dealt out , (Lysias Orator):—;Mid., ταμιεύεσθαι εἰς ὅσον βουλόμεθα ἄρχειν to control  the limits to which we mean to extend our sway, (Thucydides) 
4. of keeping house, to regulate, manage , (Aristophanes Comicus):—; Pass., χώρα ταμιευομένα τινί governed  or possessed  by one, (Pindar) 
5. to store up , (Demosthenes Orator); Ζηνὸς ταμιεύεσκε γονάς she was the depository of  it, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9400.definition:
1. to stretch, strain, stretch out , (Iliad by Homer); τ. βιόν to string  a bow, (Odyssey by Homer); and in Mid., τόξον τανυσσάμενος having strung his  bow, (Iliad by Homer):—;of putting the strings to a harp, ἐτάνυσσε χορδήν (Odyssey by Homer); τ. κανόνα to push  the weaving-bar tight , i. e. to weave, (Iliad by Homer); ὅπως τανύσηι when he reins in  [the horses, 8th/7th c.BC]; ἐπὶ Ἀκράγαντι τανύσσας (i.e. ὀϊστούς) having aimed  them, (Pindar):—;Pass., γναθμοὶ τάνυσθεν (for ἐτανύσθησαν) the hollow cheeks filled out , (Odyssey by Homer); to run at full stretch , of horses galloping, (Homer) 
2. metaphorically to strain, make more intense , μάχην (Iliad by Homer); ἔριδα πολέμοιο πεῖραρ τάνυσσαν strained  the tug of war, (Iliad by Homer) 
3. to stretch out, lay along, lay , (Homer); τ. τινὰ ἐν κονίηις, ἐπὶ γαίηι to lay  one in the dust, stretch  him at his length , (Homer):—;Pass. to lie stretched out , (Homer): to extend , (Odyssey by Homer); ἐπὶ χθονὶ κεῖτο τανυσθείς (Iliad by Homer):—;also, τρίβος τετάνυστο the path stretched away , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9402.definition:
ταπεινόφρων, -ον 
 (ταπεινός, φρήν), [in LXX: Pro.29:23 (רוּחַ שָׁפָל)* ;] 
humble-minded: 1Pe.3:8 (in bad sense, Plut., 2, 336 E, cf. Deiss., LAE, 72.3).†
 (AS)

G9403.definition:
1. troublous, turbulent , (Herdotus Historicus); ἴχνη τ. uncertain, baffling , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. troubled, disordered , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. of an army, (Thucydides) 
4. adverb, ταραχωδῶς ζῆν to live in a state of confusion , (Isocrates Orator); τ. ἔχειν πρός τινα to be rebelliously  disposed, (Demosthenes Orator); Sup. -έστατα (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G9404.definition:
Tartarus , a dark abyss, as deep below Hades as earth below heaven, the prison of the Titans, (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;later, the nether world , like Ἅιδης, (Hesiod) 
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9405.definition:
a ditch, trench , (Homer), etc.; τάφρον ὀρύσσειν (Iliad by Homer), etc.; τ. ἐλαύνειν to draw a trench , (Iliad by Homer) 
 (ML)

G9406.definition:
1. to make quickly , (Sophocles Tragicus); τοῖα σπερχόμενος ταχύνει such are the words which in his eager haste he speaks, (Euripides) 
2. intransitive to be quick, to make haste, speed, hurry , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9407.definition:
1. to stretch  by main force, to stretch to the uttermost , τόξον ἔτεινεν stretched  it to its full , (Iliad by Homer); ἐξ ἄντυγος ἡνία τείνας having tied  the reins tight  to the chariot-rail, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., [ ἱμὰς] τέτατο the strap was made tight , (Iliad by Homer); ἱστία τέτατο the sails were stretched , (Odyssey by Homer):—;absolute, μὴ τείνειν ἄγαν not to strain the cord  too tight, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. metaphorically, ἶσον τείνειν πολέμου τέλος to strain  the even tug of war, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., ἐπὶ ἶσα μάχη τέτατο (Iliad by Homer); ἵπποισι τάθη δρόμος their pace was strained to the utmost , (Iliad by Homer): also, to exert oneself, be anxious , (Pindar) 
3. to stretch out, spread , Ζεὺς λαίλαπα τείνει (Iliad by Homer); νὺξ τέταται βροτοῖσιν night is spread  over mankind, (Odyssey by Homer); so, of light, τέτατο φάος (Sophocles Tragicus); of sound, ἀμφὶ νῶτ᾽ ἐτάθη πάταγος (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. to aim at, direct towards  a point, properly from the bow, τείνειν βέλη (Sophocles Tragicus): then, metaphorically, τ. φόνον εἴς τινα to aim  death to one, design  it for him, (Euripides); τ. λόγον εἴς τινα (Plato Philosophus) 
5. to stretch out in length , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass. to lie out at length, lie stretched , ταθεὶς ἐπὶ γαίηι (Iliad by Homer); ταθεὶς ἐνὶ δεσμῶι lying stretched  in chains, (Odyssey by Homer) 
6. to stretch  or hold out, present , τινὰ ἐπὶ σφαγάν (Euripides):—;Mid., τείνεσθαι χέρε to stretch out one's  hands, etc., (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
7. to extend, lengthen , of Time, (Aeschulus Tragicus); τείνειν λόγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
8. intransitive, of geographical position, to stretch out  or extend , (Herdotus Historicus):—;of Time, τείνοντα χρόνον lengthening  time, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
9. to exert oneself, struggle , ἐναντία τινί (Plato Philosophus): to hurry on, hasten , (Euripides) 
10. to extend to, reach , Lat. pertinere, ἐπὶ τὴν ψυχήν (Plato Philosophus) 
11. to tend, refer, belong to , Lat. spectare ad, τείνει ἐς σέ it refers to, concerns  you, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ποῖ τείνε; to what tends  it? (Plato Philosophus); ἐγγύς τι τείνειν τοῦ θανάτου (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9408.definition:
enclosed by walls, beleaguered, besieged , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
 (ML)

G9409.definition:
1. to build a wall , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: with accusative cognate, τ. τεῖχος to build  it, (Thucydides); so in Mid., τεῖχος ἐτειχίσσαντο they built them  a wall, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to be built , (Pindar): 3rd singular pluperfect τετείχιστο, impersonal, buildings had been erected, there were buildings , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. transitive to wall  or fortify , τὸ οὖρος (Herdotus Historicus); τὴν πόλιν (Thucydides): in Mid., τειχίζεσθαι τὸ χωρίον (Thucydides):—;Pass. to be walled  or fenced with walls , (Thucydides); τὰ τετειχισμένα the fortified parts , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9411.definition: in Act., of the woman, to bear children , in Mid., of the man, to beget them , (Xenophon Historicus): in Mid. of both parents, to breed children , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9412.definition:
1. of a carpenter, to make, work, frame , (Iliad by Homer):—;absolute to do joiners' work , opposite to smiths' work, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. of other artificers, (Homeric Hymns) 
3. metaphorically to devise, plan, contrive , especially by craft, Lat. machinari, ἐτεκτήναντ᾽ ἀπόφθεγκτόν μ᾽ they kept me  from speech of them, (Euripides); πᾶν ἐπ᾽ ἐμοὶ τεκταινέσθω (sc. Cleon) (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. later, Act. τεκταίνω, in same sense, [variant datesAnthology Palantina, (Lucian); hence participle passive τεκταινόμενος, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9413.definition: practised  or skilled in building , (Plato Philosophus): as Substantive a good carpenter  or builder , opposite to a smith, (Xenophon Historicus): —; ἡ -κή (i.e. τέχνη); joiners' work, carpentry , (Plato Philosophus), etc. (ML)

G9414.definition:
1. a broad strap for bearing  anything 
from Root ! τλα, * τλάω, whence also the hero Telamon took his name, compare Ἄτλας 
2. a leathern strap  or belt , for bearing both shield or sword, (Homer) 
3. a broad linen bandage  for wounds, (Iliad by Homer); for swathing mummies, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9416.definition:
1. initiation  in the mysteries, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; ἐς χεῖρας ἄγεσθαι τὴν τελετήν to take in hand the matter of initiation , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural mystic rites at initiation , (Euripides), etc. 
2. a festival accompanied by such rites , in plural, (Pindar); in singular, (Euripides) (ML)

G9417.definition:
1. last , Lat. ultimus, (Herdotus Historicus); τὰ τ. the endings  or terminations , (Herdotus Historicus); τελευταίους στῆσαι to station in the rear ranks , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. of Time, ἡ τελευταία, with or without ἡμέρα, the last  day allowed for payment, (Demosthenes Orator); one's last day , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. last, uttermost , ὕβρις (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. τὸ τελευταῖον, as adverb the last time, last of all , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; or τελευταῖον (Plato Philosophus), etc.; and τὰ τελευταῖα (Thucydides) 
5. at last, in the last place , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc.: but, 
6. the adjective is often used with Verbs, where we should use the adverb, ὁ τελευταῖος δραμών (Aeschulus Tragicus); παρελθόντες τελευταῖοι (Thucydides) 
 
 (ML)

G9418.definition:
1. a piece of land cut off, assigned as a domain  to kings and chiefs, (Homer) 
2. a piece of land dedicated to a god, the sacred precincts , (Homer): in it stood the temple, (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically, the sacred valley  of the Nile is the τέμ. Νείλοιο, (Pindar); the Acropolis is the ἱερὸν τ. of Pallas, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
 (ML)

G9419.definition:
1. to cut, hew , (Homer), etc.; ὀδόντας οἵους τέμνειν teeth fit for cutting , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. to cut, wound, maim , (Iliad by Homer); πρὸς δέρην τ. to wound  her in the neck, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. of a surgeon, to cut , (Iliad by Homer): absolute to use the knife , as opposite to cautery ( κάειν), (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be operated upon , (Plato Philosophus) 
4. to cut up, cut to pieces , (Homer), etc.:—; to slaughter, sacrifice , (Iliad by Homer)

G9472.definition:

2. simply of Place, ἐν πυρῇ ὑπάτῃ on the very top  of the funeral pile, (Iliad by Homer)
