5. with genitive, like the preposition ὑπό, ὕπατος χώρας supreme over  the land, (Aeschulus Tragicus); ὕπατοι λεχέων high above  the nest, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
6. as Substantive, ὕπατος, the Roman consul , (Polybius Historicus), etc. (ML)

G9546.definition: to set up, prop up, support

G9548.definition:
1. much like ὑπερηνορέων overweening, arrogant , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. transitive to treat disdainfully , (Lucian) (ML)

G9551.definition:
1. Dep. 
2. to lie  or be situate above , (Isocrates Orator) 
3. to be postponed , (Lucian) (ML)

G9554.definition:
1. exceeding long , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἡ βασιλέος χεὶρ ὑπ. the king's arm is very long, reaches very far , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. exceeding high , of mountains, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. ὑπερμάκης βοά a cry exceeding loud , (Pindar) (ML)

G9557.definition:
ὑπερ-οράω, see: ὑπερεῖδον.
 ὑπερ-εῖδον, aor. 
 [in LXX for עָלַם hi., מַעַל, etc. ;] 
to overlook: with accusative of thing(s), Act.17:30 
 (AS)

G9559.definition:
1. to set higher, erect , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. to set on the other side, carry over , (Plutarch) 
3. in Mid. to hold over , so as to protect, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. metaphorically, παντὶ θεὸν ὑπερτιθέμεν to set  God over  all, (Pindar) 
5. to communicate  a thing to another, ὑπερετίθεα (ionic imperfect for -ετίθην); τὰ ἔμελλον ποιήσειν (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid., especially in order to ask advice, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9561.definition:
1. to bear  or carry over  a place, ὑπ. τὸν ἰσθμὸν τὰς ναῦς (Thucydides):—;Pass., [ αἱ ναῦς] αἱ ὑπερενεχθεῖσαι τὸν ἰσθμόν (Thucydides) 
2. intransitive to rise above, to surpass, excel, have the advantage over , τινός τινι one in a thing, (Herdotus Historicus); also with accusative pro genitive, ὑπερφέρεις τόλμῃ τόλμαν (Euripides): absolute to excel, have preeminence , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9565.definition:
1. liable to give account for  one's administration  of an office, accountable, responsible , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—; ὑπεύθυνοι, οἱ, at Athens, magistrates who had to submit their accounts  to public auditors  λογισταί); (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. 
2. with genitive responsible for , ὑπ. ἀρχῆς ἑτέρας quoted in (Demosthenes Orator); of slaves, σῶμα ὑπ. ἀδικημάτων their body is liable for  their misdeeds, i. e. they must pay for  them with their body, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. with dative responsible to  another, dependent on  them, Lat. obnoxius, (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9566.definition:
1. the body of rowers and sailors, the ship's crew , (Thucydides), etc. 
2. service , (Aristophanes Comicus), etc. (ML)

G9567.definition: to put to sleep :—; Pass. to fall asleep, sleep , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9569.definition: to look up from under  the brows at, glance at, to look askance at, eye suspiciously  or angrily , Lat. limis oculis suspicere, (Plato Philosophus); also ὑπ. ἐλεεινά to cast  piteous glances , [variant datesAnthology Palantina:—;Pass. to be looked at with suspicion , (Euripides) (ML)

G9571.definition: a garment under a coat of mail , (Plutarch) (ML)

G9573.definition:
1. to burn by applying fire below , (Herdotus Historicus): to offer secret sacrifices , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. to light under , (Lucian) (ML)

G9576.definition:
1. to lie under  or beneath , (Iliad by Homer); with dative, (Plato Philosophus) 
2. in various metaphorically senses, 
3. to be put under  the eyes or mind, i. e. to be submitted  or proposed to one , (Pindar); αἱ ὑποκείμεναι ἐλπίδες one's present  hopes, (Demosthenes Orator); ὑπόκειταί μοι ὅτι . . I have laid down the rule , that . ., (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. to be laid down  or assumed as an hypothesis , (Plato Philosophus), etc.; τούτων ὑποκειμένων = Lat. his positis, (Plato Philosophus); impersonal, ὑπόκειται a rule is laid down , (Demosthenes Orator); ὑποκείσθω ὅτι . . let it be granted  that . ., (Aristotle Philosopher) 
5. to be suggested , (Herdotus Historicus) 
6. to be left at bottom, left remaining , (Thucydides) 
7. to be subject to, submit to , τινι (Plato Philosophus): absolute to be submissive , (Plato Philosophus) 
8. to be left behind in pledge, to be pledged  or mortgaged , τινος for  a certain sum, (Demosthenes Orator), etc.; ὑποκείμενοι, of persons, bound for payment  of a sum of money, (Demosthenes Orator) 
9. to underlie , as a substratum, (Plato Philosophus), etc. 
10. to be subordinate , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9577.definition:
ὑπό-λειμμα 
 (WH, -λιμμα, see their App., 154), -τος, τό, [in LXX chiefly for שָׁאַר ;] 
a remnant: Rom.9:27 (Arist., al.; cf. κατάλειμμα).†
 (AS)

G9578.definition:
1. left behind, staying behind , (Herdotus Historicus); οἱ ὑπ. those who remained alive , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. of things, ὑπ. τὸ βάραθρον γίγνεται the pit still remains , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὅσα ἦν ὑπ. all that remained to be done , (Thucydides) (ML)

G9580.definition:
1. to loosen beneath  or below , ὑπέλυσε γυῖα made  his limbs give way under him , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., γυῖα ὑπέλυντο (Iliad by Homer) 
2. to loose from under  the yoke, (Homer):—; to loose from bonds , (Odyssey by Homer); in Mid., τὸν ὑπελύσαο δεσμῶν thou didst free  him from bonds by stealth , (Iliad by Homer) 
3. to untie  a person's sandals from under  his feet, take off  his shoes, (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Mid. to take off one's  sandals or shoes, or to have  them taken off , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
4. with accusative pers. to unshoe  him, take off  his shoes , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9581.definition:
1. a remembrance, memorial , (Thucydides), etc. 
2. a note, memorandum , (Demosthenes Orator):—;in plural memoranda, notes, minutes , Lat. commentarii, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9584.definition: to prick  or sting underneath : generally, to sting , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9585.definition:
1. to fall under  or down, to sink in , (Plutarch) 
2. to fall down before  any one, with accusative, (Plato Philosophus): —;hence, to be subject  to him, fall under  his power, (Isocrates Orator); of a flatterer, to cringe to , τινί (Demosthenes Orator); with accusative ὑποπεσὼν τὸν δεσπότην (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to fall behind  another, (Demosthenes Orator) 
4. to get in under  or among , (Thucydides) 
5. of accidents, to happen, fall out , (Isocrates Orator) 
6. of persons, to fall under  a punishment, with dative, (Plutarch) 
7. of places, to lie under  or below , with dative, (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9586.definition:
1. to be suspicious , (Xenophon Historicus); also, ὑπ. εἴς τινα to have suspicions  of him, (Thucydides) 
2. to suspect, guess, suppose , (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. transitive to suspect, hold in suspicion , (Sophocles Tragicus); ὑπ. τινὰ εἴς τι of something, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be suspected, mistrusted , (Thucydides); impersonal, ὡς ὑπωπτεύετο as was generally suspected , (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. with accusative pers. et infinitive to suspect that , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
5. with accusative rei, to look suspiciously on , (Thucydides):—;but also, ὑπ. τι to suspect  something, (Euripides) 
from ὑπόπτης (ML)

G9588.definition:
1. to trip up one's heels, upset , Lat. supplantare, (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. metaphorically, ὑπ. καὶ ἀνατρέπων (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9594.definition: rendering service, serviceable, promoting, conducive to  a thing, with dative, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9595.definition: a light shewing through a small hole: a narrow opening , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9597.definition:
1. under the hand, in hand , (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. of persons, under  any one's hand, under command, subject , τινι (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; λαβεῖν τινα ὑποχείριον to get into one's power , (Euripides); ἔχειν τινὰ ὑπ. (Thucydides) (ML)

G9599.definition:
1. indebted, in debt , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὑπ. τινος his debtor , (Plutarch) 
2. of property, involved , Lat. obaeratus, (Demosthenes Orator) 
3. with genitive, ὑπ. φιλίας bound by ties of  friendship, (Plutarch) (ML)

G9601.gloss: to turn up and open hands
G9601.definition: to bend oneself back, to carry one's head high , (Aeschines Orator):—;Pass., κάρα ὑπτιάζεται his head lies supine , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9602.definition:
1. laid back, laid on one's back , πέσεν ὕπτιος he fell backwards , opposite to πρηνής, (Iliad by Homer); of a quadruped, ὀρθοῦ ἑστεῶτος καὶ ὑπτίου rearing upright and falling backwards , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. generally with the under side uppermost , χείρ ὑπτία the hollow of  the hand, (Plutarch); ἐξ ὑπτίου κράνους from the upturned  helmet, with the hollow uppermost , (Aeschulus Tragicus); so, παράθες ὑπτίαν  τὴν ἀσπίδα); (Aristophanes Comicus); ἀψὶς ὑπτία a half-wheel with the concave side uppermost , (Herdotus Historicus); ὑπτίοις σέλμασιν ναυτίλλεται he sails with the bottom uppermost , i. e. suffers shipwreck, (Sophocles Tragicus); ἐξ ὑπτίας νεῖν to swim on the back  (in metaphorically sense), (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of land, sloping evenly , of Egypt, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9605.definition:
1. to weave , ἱστὸν ὑφαίνειν to weave  a web, (Homer); ἱμάτιον (Plato Philosophus), etc.:—;absolute to weave, ply the loom , (Herdotus Historicus):—;Mid., ἱμάτιον ὑφαίνεσθαι to weave oneself  a cloak, (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to contrive, plan, invent , Lat. texere, δόλον ὑφαίνειν (Iliad by Homer); μῆτιν ὑφ. (Odyssey by Homer) 
3. generally, to create, construct , (Pindar) (ML)

G9606.definition:
1. to seize underneath  or inwardly , (Homer) 
2. to draw  or take away from under  a thing, with genitive, (Iliad by Homer):—;also τὴν χεῖρα ὑφῄρει tried to draw  it away , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. to take away underhand, filch away , (Thucydides); ὑφ. τῆς ὑποψίας gradually to take away  part of . ., (Thucydides):—;Pass., ὑπαραιρημένος (ionic perfect participle) put secretly away, made away with , (Herdotus Historicus):—;so in Mid. to take away underhand, filch away, purloin , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
4. in Mid. also with accusative pers., ὑφ. τινά τινος to rob  him of a thing, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9609.definition:
1. in these tenses Causal, to place  or set under , τί τινι (Herdotus Historicus); τρεῖς σταυροὺς ὑπίστησι plants  three piles in the lake to support  a house, (Herdotus Historicus):—;metaphorically, γνώμας ὑποστήσας σοφάς having laid  them as a foundation , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. to post secretly  or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. Causal also in future and aor1 middle to substitute , τί τινι one thing for  another, (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. Pass., with aorist2  active ὑπ-έστην, perfect ὑφ-έστηκα, ionic participle ὑπ-εστεώς:—; to stand under as a support , with dative, (Herdotus Historicus) 
5. to sink to the bottom, settle , τὸ ὑφιστάμενον the milk, opposite to τὸ ἐφιστάμενον (the cream), (Herdotus Historicus) 
6. to place oneself under an engagement, engage  or promise  to do, with infinitive future, ὅσς᾽ Ἀχιλῆι ὑπέστημεν δώσειν (Iliad by Homer), etc.; with infinitive aorist, οὔ τίς με ὑπέστη σαῶσαι (Iliad by Homer); with infinitive present, (Herdotus Historicus):—;absolute, after promise given , (Odyssey by Homer); ὥσπερ ὑπέστη as he promised , (Thucydides):—;when followed by accusative, an infinitive may be supplied, τρίποδας οὕς οἱ ὑπέστη (i.e. δώσειν); (Iliad by Homer); ἐκτελέουσιν ὑπόσχεσιν ἥνπερ ὑπέσταν (Iliad by Homer) 
7. to submit  to any one, τινι (Iliad by Homer) 
8. with accusative rei, to submit to, consent to , ὁ τὸ ἐλάχιστον ὑπιστάμενος who offers to take  the least, (Herdotus Historicus); ὑφ. τὸν πλοῦν to undertake  it unwillingly , (Thucydides); so, ὑφ. τὸν κίνδυνον (Thucydides): —;rarely with dative, ὑφ. ξυμφοραῖς ταῖς μεγίσταις (Thucydides) 
9. to undertake  an office, (Xenophon Historicus) 
10. to lie concealed  or in ambush , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
11. to support an attack, to resist, withstand , with dative, (Aeschulus Tragicus); with accusative, (Euripides):—;absolute to stand one's ground, face the enemy , Lat. subsistere, (Euripides) (ML)

G9612.definition:
1. to send rain, to rain , Ζεὺς ὗε (Homer), etc.; ὁ θεὸς ὕει (Herdotus Historicus):—;then, the nom. being omitted, ὕει used impersonal, Lat. pluit, it rains, (Hesiod); ὕοντος when it is raining , (Aristophanes Comicus); ὕοντος πολλῷ as it was raining  heavily, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. with accusative loci, ἑπτὰ ἐτέων οὐκ ὗε τὴν Θήρην for seven years it did  not rain on  Thera, (Herdotus Historicus):—;hence in Pass., with future middle to be rained on , (Odyssey by Homer); ὕσθησαν αἱ Θῆβαι Thebes was rained upon , i. e. it rained there, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡ χώρη ὕεται, i. e. it rains  in the country, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. with accusative cognate, ὗσε χρυσόν it rained  gold, (Pindar); καινὸν ἀεὶ Ζεὺς ὕει ὕδωρ (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9613.definition: dusky, dun, gray , Lat. fuscus, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9614.definition:
lentil , and its fruit , (Herdotus Historicus), etc. 
 (ML)

G9615.definition: baldheaded, bald , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; πρόσωπον φαλακρόν (Euripides) (ML)

G9617.definition: a quiver  for arrows, Lat. pharetra, (Homer) (ML)

G9618.definition:
1. to administer a drug , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. to use enchantments , φαρμακεύειν τι ἐς τὸν ποταμόν to use  it as a charm to calm  the river, (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. with accusative pers. to drug, give  him a poisonous  or stupefying drug , (Euripides) (ML)

G9619.definition:
φάρμακον, -ου, τό, 
 [in LXX for כֶּשֶׁף ;] 
 __(a) a drug; 
 __(b) an in­cantation, enchantment: Rev.9:21, Tr., mg., WH, txt. (RV, sorceries).†
 (AS)

G9621.definition: the throat, gullet , (Odyssey by Homer), etc. (ML)

G9623.definition:
1. an apparition, phantom , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; φ. ἀνδρός the spectral appearance  of a man, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a vision  in a dream, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc. 
2. a sign from heaven, portent, omen , (Herdotus Historicus); periphrastic, φάσμα ταύρου a monster  of a bull, (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9626.definition: to hold cheap, to depreciate, disparage , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9631.definition: that which is brought by the wife  (compare ἕδνον); a dowry, portion , Lat. dos, (Herdotus Historicus); also in plural of a dower , as consisting of divers presents, (Euripides); but, φερναὶ πολέμου, of a wife won in battle, (Euripides):—;in plural, also, bridal gifts , (Euripides) (ML)

G9634.definition:
1. the sound of the voice, a voice , (Pindar), etc.: of a person, ὦ φθέγμ᾽ ἀναιδές, for ὦ φθεγξάμενε ἀναιδῆ, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
2. language, speech , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. a saying, word , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. of other sounds, as of birds, cries , (Sophocles Tragicus); of a bull, roaring , (Euripides); φθ. θυείας the grinding  of the mortar, (Aristophanes Comicus); of the nightingale's song, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9640.definition: fond of a country life , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9642.definition:
1. to be fond of strife, engage in eager rivalry, be contentious , φιλονεικῶν out of contentiousness  or party spirit , (Thucydides); φ. πρός τινα (Lysias Orator):—;with accusative, φ. τὸ ἐμὲ εἶναι τὸν ἀποκρινόμενον to be eager  that I should be the answerer, (Plato Philosophus); τὰ χείρω φ. to be so obstinate as to choose  the worst, (Thucydides) 
2. in good sense, to struggle emulously , φ. περὶ τῶν καλλίστων (Isocrates Orator) (ML)

G9643.definition:
1. a muzzle , Lat. capistrum, (Lucian) 
2. the nose-band  of a horse's bridle, fitted with pipes through which the horses' breath made a whistling sound, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. a kind of cup , used as a dice-box , Lat. fritillus, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9644.definition: to be heated, inflamed, to fester , φλεγμαίνουσα πόλις, opposite to ὑγιής, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9645.definition:
1. transitive to burn, burn up , (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass. to take fire, blaze up , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. metaphorically to kindle, inflame  with passion, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass., like Lat. uri, to burn with passion, be inflamed, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. to light up , Ζεὺς βέλος φλέγων making  it blaze  or flash , (Aeschulus Tragicus); metaphorically, ἄταν οὐρανίαν φλέγων letting  the flame of mischief blaze up  to heaven, (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to blaze up, be a-light , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. metaphorically to make illustrious  or famous , Lat. illustrare, (Pindar):—;Pass. to be  or become so , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. intransitive to burn, flame, blaze , (Aeschulus Tragicus); of armour, to flash , (Euripides) 
6. metaphorically to break forth , of passion, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
7. to shine forth, become famous , (Pindar) (ML)

G9646.definition:
1. a vein , (Iliad by Homer), etc.; φλέβα σχάζειν to open a vein , (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. a vein  of metal, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9647.definition: in plural φλιαί, = σταθμοί, the doorposts, jambs , (Odyssey by Homer); in singular, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9653.definition: purple-red, purple  or crimson , and (generally) red , Lat. puniceus, (Herdotus Historicus):—;attic contracted φοινι-κοῦς, ᾶ, οῦν, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9662.definition:
1. a shuddering, shivering , (Plato Philosophus) 
2. shuddering , especially from religious awe, (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9664.definition: that causes shuddering, horrible , (Euripides):—;neuter φρικῶδες, as adverb horribly , (Euripides):—; adverb -δῶς, Sup., φρικωδέστατα ἔχειν to be in utter horror , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9665.definition:
1. thought, care, heed, attention  bestowed upon a person or thing, with genitive, φροντίδ᾽ ἔχειν τινός (Euripides); ἐν φροντίδι εἶναι περί τινος (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. absolute thought, meditation , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐν φροντίδι μοι ἐγένετο [ τὸ πρῆγμα] (Herdotus Historicus); ἐμβῆσαί τινα ἐς φροντίδα to set one a thinking , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.:—;in plural thoughts , αἱ δεύτεραί πως φροντίδες σοφώτεραι (Euripides) 
3. deep thought, care, concern , (Aeschulus Tragicus); οὐ φροντὶς Ἱπποκλείδῃ no matter  to Hippocleides! (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9666.definition:
1. a looking out, watch, guard , as a duty, (Herdotus Historicus); φρουρὰν ἄζηλον ὀχήσω shall keep unenviable watch , (Aeschulus Tragicus); φρουρὰ ὄμματος my watchful eye, (Sophocles Tragicus); φρουρᾶς ᾄδειν to sing while on guard , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. a prison , (Plato Philosophus) 
3. of persons, a watch, guard, garrison , (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; especially of frontier-posts , which were guarded in Attica by the περίπολοι, (Xenophon Historicus) 
4. at Sparta, a body of men destined for service , φρουρὰν φαίνειν (see. φαίνω A. 1. 5). (ML)

G9668.definition:
1. a violent snorting, neighing , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. metaphorically wanton behaviour, insolence , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9670.definition:
1. to roast  or fry , (Aristophanes Comicus); ἐρετμοῖσι φρύξουσι they shall cook  with the [wood of] the oars, (Oracle quoted in Herdotus Historicus):—;Pass., πεφρυγμέναι κριθαί roasted  barley, (Thucydides) 
2. of the sun, to parch , Lat. torrere, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (ML)

G9674.definition: to drive from a country, banish , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9675.definition:
1. one who flees  from his country, a runaway, fugitive, a banished man, exile, refugee , Lat. exul, profugus, (Herdotus Historicus), attic; φυγάδα ποιεῖν τινα (Xenophon Historicus); κατάγειν φυγάδας to recall them; etc. 
2. of an army, put to flight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9676.definition:
1. growth, stature , especially fine growth, noble stature , (Homer); Νέστορι εἶδός τε μέγεθός τε φυήν τt ἄγχιστα ἐῴκει he was like Nestor both in shape and size and stature  (or growth) , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. poetry for φύσις, one's natural powers, nature, genius , (Pindar) 
3. the flower  or prime of age , (Pindar) (ML)

G9679.definition:
1. the chief of a  φυ_λή, a phylarch , (Herdotus Historicus):—;used to translated the Rom. tribunus , (Plutarch) 
2. at Athens, the commander of the cavalry furnished by each tribe , see. ἵππαρχος. (ML)

G9681.definition:
1. to mix  flour or meal so as to make  it into dough, to knead , (Herdotus Historicus); γῆν φυράσειν φόνῳ to make  earth into a  bloody paste , (Aeschulus Tragicus):—;Pass., οἴνῳ καὶ ἐλαίῳ πεφυραμένα ἄλφιτα (Thucydides) 
2. metaphorically, μαλακὴν φωνὴν φυράσασθαι to make up  a soft voice, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9683.definition:
1. to mix  something dry with  something wet , mostly with a sense of mixing so as to soil  or defile , δάκρυσιν εἵματ᾽ ἔφυρον they wetted, sullied  their garments with tears, (Iliad by Homer); also with genitive, χείλεα φύρσω αἵματος (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., δάκρυσι πεφυρμένη (Iliad by Homer); αἵματι οἶκος ἐφύρθη (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. of dry things, κόνει φύρουσα κάρα (Euripides); γαίαι πεφύρσεσθαι κόμαν to be doomed to have  one's hair defiled  with earth, (Pindar) 
3. metaphorically to mingle together, confuse , ἔφυρον εἰκῆ πάντα they mixed  all things up together, did all at random, (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;Pass. to be mixed up , ἐκ πεφυρμένου καὶ θηριώδους from a confused  and savage state, (Euripides) 
4. in Pass. also to mix with others, have dealings with  him, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9684.definition:
1. transitive to puff  or blow up, distend , (Aristophanes Comicus); of bag-pipers, (Aristophanes Comicus); φ. τὰς γνάθους to puff  them out , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be inflated , ἡ γαστὴρ ἐπεφύσητό μοι (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. metaphorically to puff  one up, make  him vain , and so to cheat , (Demosthenes Orator):—;Pass. to be puffed up , ἐπί τινι at a thing, (Xenophon Historicus) 
3. to blow up, kindle  a fire: but also 
4. to blow out, extinguish , τὴν λαμπάδα (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. to blow out, spurt out , (Sophocles Tragicus) 
6. to blow  a wind-instrument, (Euripides) (ML)

G9685.definition: an instrument for blowing, blowpipe  or tube , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

G9687.definition:
1. that which has grown, a plant, tree , (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
2. generally a creature , of men, (Euripides) 
3. like ἔρνος, of men, a descendant, child , (Euripides) (ML)

G9688.definition:
1. to search after a thief  or theft, search a house , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. in Pass. to be detected , (Demosthenes Orator); with participle, κλέπτης ὢν φωρᾶσθαι (Demosthenes Orator); so, κακὸς [ ὢν] ἐφωράθη φίλοις (Euripides):—;also of things, ἀργύριον ἐφωράθη ἐξαγόμενον money was discovered  to be in course of exportation, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9693.definition:
1. a small stone, pebble , in plural, (Lucian), etc. 
2. as collect. in singular, gravel, rubble , used in building, (Thucydides); so also in plural, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9694.definition:
1. a smith's shop, forge, smithy , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. = χαλκίον, a copper, caldron , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. a metal reflector  in a lamp, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9695.definition: of copper  or bronze, brasen , (Homer); χαλκήιος δόμος, = χαλκεῖον, a forge , (Odyssey by Homer); χάλκειον γένος, of the Age of brass , (Hesiod) (ML)

G9696.definition:
1. to make of copper  or (generally) of metal, to forge , (Iliad by Homer), etc.:—;Mid. to forge for oneself , (Theognis Elegiacus):—;Pass. to be wrought  or forged , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. absolute to be a smith, work as a smith, ply the hammer , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ χαλκεύειν the smith's art , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9697.definition: the chameleon , a kind of lizard known for changing its colour, (Aristotle Philosopher) (ML)

G9698.definition:
1. chaos , the first stateof the universe, (Hesiod), etc. 
2. infinite space, the expanse , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
3. the nether abyss, infinite darkness , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9699.definition: perhaps a yellowish bird dwelling in clefts the curlew , (Aristophanes Comicus): χαραδριοῦ βίον ζῆν, of a glutton, (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9701.definition: to fence by a palisade, fortify , (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9703.definition:
1. to make sharp  or pointed, sharpen, whet , (Hesiod) 
2. to furnish with notches  or teeth , like a saw, (Aristotle Philosopher):—;Pass., σκύταλον κεχ. ὄζοις a staff jagged  or rugged  with branches, (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus): metaphorically, [ ὄμμα] ἠλεμάτοις ἀκτῖσι χαράσσεται sparkles  with false lights, of the effect produced by painting the eye-lids, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
3. metaphorically in Pass., κεχαραγμένος τινί exasperated at  any one, (Herdotus Historicus); κείνῳ τόδε μὴ χαράσσου be not angry at  him for  this, (Euripides) 
4. to cut into furrows, cut, scratch , (Pindar):—;Pass., κέκοπται καὶ χαράσσεται πέδον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. to engrave, inscribe , [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9704.definition:
1. a joy , (Euripides); plural joys, delights , (Euripides) 
2. = χάρμα II, joy, delight , (Sophocles Tragicus) (ML)

G9710.definition:
1. of  or in winter, of  or in winter-time , opposite to θερινός, χ. τροπαί (see. τροπή 1), (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὴν χ. (i.e. ὥρην); during the winter season , (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. wintry , (Thucydides); see. χειμέριος. (ML)

G9712.definition:
1. a voting  or electing by show of hands , (Thucydides) 
2. a vote , Lat. suffragium, in plural, (Aeschines Orator) (ML)

G9713.definition:
1. to bring into hand, to manage, master, subdue , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. mostly in Mid., to conquer, overpower, subdue , (Herdotus Historicus); so, τήνδ᾽ ἐχειρούμην ἄγραν became master of  this booty, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. without any sense of violence, to master, subdue , (Xenophon Historicus), etc. 
4. χειροῦμαι is also Pass. to be subdued , [variant datesTragica Adespota; future χειρωθήσομαι (Demosthenes Orator); aor1 ἐχειρώθην (Herdotus Historicus); perfect κεχείρωμαι (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9714.definition:
1. the swallow , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; the twittering of the swallow was proverbially used of barbarous tongues by the Greeks, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χελιδόνων μουσεῖα (see. μουσεῖον);  proverbs also, μία χελιδὼν ἔαρ οὐ ποιεῖ (Aristotle Philosopher) 
2. the frog in a horse's foot , so called from its being forked like the swallow's tail , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9715.definition:
1. a tortoise , (Homeric Hymns); prov. of insensibility, ἰὼ χελῶναι μακάριαι τοῦ δέρματος oh ye tortoises , happy in your thick skins! (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. like Roman testudo, a pent-house formed of shields overlapping each other like the scales on a tortoise's back , used by storming parties in approaching a city's walls: then, generally, a pent-house  for protecting besiegers, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9718.definition: on  or of dry land , ὄρνιθες χ. land- birds, opposite to λιμναῖοι, (Herdotus Historicus); χ. κροκόδειλος a lizard, (Herdotus Historicus):—;also of landsmen , as opposite to seamen, (Euripides); κῦμα χερσαῖον στρατοῦ, an army, opposite to a fleet, (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9719.definition:
1. dry land, land , ἐπὶ χέρσου, opposite to ἐν πόντῳ, (Odyssey by Homer); κύματα κυλινδόμενα προτὶ χέρσον (Odyssey by Homer); κῦμα χέρσῳ ῥηγνύμενον (Iliad by Homer); χέρσῳ on  or by land , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. as adjective, χέρσος, ον, dry, firm , of land, (Herdotus Historicus); ἐν κονίᾳ χέρσῳ, opposite to πόντῳ, (Pindar) 
3. dry, hard, barren , (Herdotus Historicus); χ. λιμήν a harbour left dry , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
4. metaphorically barren, without children , of women, (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive barren of , πυρὰ χέρσος ἀγλαϊσμάτων (Euripides) 
Prob. from same Root as ξηρός. (ML)

G9721.definition:
1. Radic. sense, to pour : 
2. properly of liquids, to pour out, pour , (Homer), etc.; Zeus χέει ὕδωρ, i. e. he makes it rain, (Iliad by Homer); χέει χιόνα βορέας (Euripides); absolute, χέει it snows , (Iliad by Homer):—;Mid. to pour for oneself , especially of drink-offerings, χοὰς χεόμην νεκύεσσι (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;Pass., χέονται κρῆναι they gush forth , (Euripides); χυθέντος ποτοῦ ἐς γῆν (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. χ. δάκρυα to shed  tears, (Iliad by Homer):—;Pass., of tears, to pour  or gush forth , (Homer); so of blood, to be shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. in Pass. to become liquid, melt, thaw , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. of solids, to shed, scatter , φύλλα (Iliad by Homer); πτερά (Odyssey by Homer); χ. κόνιν κὰκ κεφαλῆς (Homer); χ. καλάμην χθονί, of a mower or reaper (see. καλάμη), (Iliad by Homer) 
6. like χώννυμι, to throw out  earth, so as to form a mound, σῆμα, τύμβον χ. (Homer) 
7. χ. δοῦρα to pour  or shower  spears, (Iliad by Homer); Mid., βέλεα χέοντο they showered their  arrows, (Iliad by Homer) 
8. to let fall  or drop , ἡνία (Iliad by Homer); so, χέειν κρόκου βαφὰς (see. βαφή II) (Aeschulus Tragicus); but, καρπὸν χ., of trees, to produce  fruit abundantly , (Odyssey by Homer) 
9. in Pass. to be thrown  or heaped up together , (Homer) 
10. in Pass. also of living beings, to pour  or stream in a dense mass  or throng , (Homer) 
11. metaphorically of sounds, to pour forth , φωνήν, αὐδήν (Odyssey by Homer); φθόγγον (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
12. of things that obscure the sight, κατ᾽ ὀφθαλμῶν χέεν ἀχλύν shed  a dark cloud over the eyes, (Iliad by Homer); πολλὴν ἠέρα χεῦε shed  a mist abroad, (Odyssey by Homer):—;Pass., ἀμφὶ δέ οἱ θάνατος χύτο was shed  around him, (Iliad by Homer); νόσος κέχυται (Sophocles Tragicus); φρὶξ ἐπὶ πόντον ἐχεύατο (Mid. in passive sense), (Iliad by Homer) 
13. of persons, ἀμφ᾽ αὐτῶι χυμένη throwing herself  around him, (Homer): so in Mid., ἀμφὶ υἱὸν ἐχεύατο πήχεε (Iliad by Homer) 
14. perfect passive κέχυμαι, to be wholly engaged in , Δᾶλος, ἐν ἇι κέχυμαι (Pindar) (ML)

G9722.definition:
1. a horse's hoof , (Hesiod):—;also, a cloven hoof , (Euripides) 
2. in plural, of the talons  of a bird, [variant datesTragica Adespota; of a wolf's claws , (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) 
3. a sea-bank, breakwater , formed of stones laid at the base of a sea-wall, to break the force of the waves (so called because it projected like a hoof) , Lat. crepido, (Thucydides) 
4. the spur of a mountain  or ridge of rocks  answering a like purpose, (Thucydides) 
5. a cloven implement , such as a netting-needle;—;  compare χηλεύω. (ML)

G9725.definition:
1. intransitive to be bereaved  of a person or thing, with genitive, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. absolute to be bereaved of a husband, to be widowed, live in widowhood , (Demosthenes Orator), etc.;—;of a man, to be a widower , (Plutarch); so, χηρεύσει λέχος (Euripides) 
3. to live in solitude , of an exile, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
4. transitive to bereave , (Euripides) (ML)

G9726.definition: of yesterday , τὸ χθιζὸν χρεῖος their yesterday's  debt, (Iliad by Homer); ὁ χθ. πόνος yesterday's  labour, (Herdotus Historicus); in adverbial sense, with Verbs, χθιζὸς ἔβη he went yesterday , (Iliad by Homer); χθ. ἤλυθες (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—;neuter χθιζόν as adverb = χθές, (Homer); so plural χθιζά, see. πρώιζος. (ML)

G9727.definition:
1. the earth, ground , (Homer); χθόνα δῦναι to go beneath the earth , i. e. to die, (Iliad by Homer); κατὰ χθονὸς κρύπτειν τινά (Sophocles Tragicus); κούφα σοι χθὼν ἐπάνω πέσοι (Euripides) 
2. of the nether world , οἱ ὑπὸ χθονός, i. e. those in the shades below , Lat. inferi, (Aeschulus Tragicus); κατὰ χθονὸς θεαί, i. e. the Erinyes, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
3. earth , i. e. the whole earth, the world , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
4. Earth , as a goddess, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
5. a particular land  or country , of Ithaca, (Odyssey by Homer); of Libya, (Pindar); χθὼν Ἀσιᾶτις, Δωρίς, Ἀργεία, Ἑλλάς, Ἰδαία, etc., [variant datesTragica Adespota (ML)

G9728.definition: unripe wheaten groats , as ἄλφιτα are barley-groats, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9729.definition:
1. the office  or post  of χιλίαρχος, (Xenophon Historicus) 
2. the office of the tribuni militares , (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

G9732.definition:
1. a she-goat , Lat. capra, (Iliad by Homer), attic 
2. Χίμαιρα, ἡ, Chimaera , a firespouting-monster, with lion's head, serpent's tail, and goat's body, killed by Bellerophon, (Iliad by Homer) (ML)

G9733.definition:
1. a he-goat , Lat. caper, = τράγος, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. also feminine = χίμαιρα, [Refs 3rd c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9735.definition:
Lat. laena, a large square upper-garment, a cloak, mantle, (Homer); it was made of wool, and worn over the χιτών, thrown over the shoulders, fastened with a pin or brooch  περόνη). It is also called φᾶρος by (Homer), and in later Greek ἱμάτιον, Latin pallium.  
derivation uncertain (ML)

G9741.definition:
1. any light porous substance , ἁλὸς χνόος the foam that gathers at the edge  of the sea, (Odyssey by Homer); πωλικὸς χν. horse's foam , [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. the first down on the chin  of youths, Lat. lanugo, (Aristophanes Comicus): the bloom  on fruit, [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9744.definition:
1. like χόλη, gall, bile , (Iliad by Homer) 
2. generally metaphorically bile, gall, bitter anger, wrath , (Homer), attic; χόλος ἔδυ τινά (Iliad by Homer); χόλος ἔμπεσε θυμῷ (Iliad by Homer); χόλον πέσσειν, καταπέσσειν (see. entry); χ. σβέσσαι παῦσαι (Iliad by Homer); χόλου παύεσθαι (Hesiod):—;with genitive objecti, anger towards  or because of  another, (Iliad by Homer); with genitive rei, anger for, because of  a thing, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. an object of anger , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9746.definition:
1. gut-string, the string  of a lyre, Lat. chorda, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. tripe , (Batrachomyomachia): also = χόρδευμα, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9747.definition:
1. to dance a round  or choral dance , (Sophocles Tragicus), etc.; especially of the Bacchic chorus, (Euripides):—; to take part in the chorus , regarded as a matter of religion, (Sophocles Tragicus): to be one of a chorus , (Aristophanes Comicus): —;with dative pers. to dance to  him, in  his honour , (Euripides) 
2. generally, to dance , especially from joy, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
3. metaphorically to practise  a thing, be versed  in it, (Plato Philosophus) 
4. with accusative cognate, φροίμιον χορεύσομαι I will dance  a prelude (to festivities), (Aeschulus Tragicus); χ. γάμους to celebrate  them, (Euripides); ὄργια Μουσῶν (Aristophanes Comicus):—;Mid., χορεύεσθαι δίνας to ply the  eddying dance , (Euripides):—;Pass., κεχόρευται ἡμῖν (sings the Chorus) our part is played , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
5. transitive to celebrate in choral dance , Ἴακχον (Sophocles Tragicus):—;Pass. to be celebrated in choral dance , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
6. Causal, to set  one a dancing, to rouse, wake to the dance , τινά (Euripides); so, πόδα χορεύειν [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9748.definition:
1. the office of a  χορηγός at Athens, the defraying of the cost of the public choruses , being the chief of the λειτουργίαι, (Thucydides), etc. 
2. means for providing  χοροί: abundance of means, fortune , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. metaphorically supplies for war , (Polybius Historicus) (ML)

G9749.definition: the membrane that encloses the fetus, the afterbirth , Lat. secundae: plural χόρια, ων, τά, a dish made by stuffing it with honey and milk , a kind of haggis , (Aristophanes Comicus): proverbial, χαλεπὸν χορίω (doric genitive) κύνα γεῦσαι don't let a dog taste blood,  (Theocritus Poeta Bucolicus) (cf. Horace, canis a corio nunquam absterrebitur uncto).  (ML)

G9751.definition: a being fed, feasting , [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9753.definition: a coos, a measurement of liquid (Lev.19.36)

G9754.definition:
to neigh, whinny , Lat. hinnire, of horses, (Iliad by Homer), etc. 
Formed from the sound. (ML)

G9756.definition:
1. that which one needs must pay, an obligation, debt , (Odyssey by Homer); a debt for stolen cattle , (Iliad by Homer); χρεῖος ἀποστήσασθαι to pay a debt  in full, (Iliad by Homer); ἀρᾶς τίνει χρ. pays the debt demanded by  the curse, (Aeschulus Tragicus); χρέος πόλει προσάπτειν to attach a further debt , i.e. guilt  to the city, (Sophocles Tragicus); χρέος ἀποδιδόναι to repay a debt , (Herdotus Historicus):—;in plural debts , χρειῶν λύσις (Hesiod); τὴν οὐσίαν ἅπασαν χρέα κατέλιπε left all the property in outstanding debts , (Demosthenes Orator) 
2. a needful business, an affair, matter , ἑὸν αὐτοῦ χρεῖος (Odyssey by Homer): a requirement, a purpose , (Sophocles Tragicus): with genitive, like χάριν, for the sake of , σὸν οὐκ ἔλασσον ἢ κείνης χρέος (Euripides) 
3. like χρῆμα, a thing , τί χρέο; = τί χρῆμ; wherefore?  (Aeschulus Tragicus); ἐφ᾽ ὅ τι χρ. ἐμόλετ; (Euripides) 
4. in (Odyssey by Homer), ἦλθον Τειρεσίαο κατὰ χρέος seems to be = Τειρεσίᾳ χρησόμενος, I came to consult  him:—;but, κατὰ χρέος according to what is due , as is meet , (Homeric Hymns) 
5. a duty, task, charge, office , (Pindar) (ML)

G9757.definition:
to utter oracles, divine , (Aristophanes Comicus) 
from χρησμολόγος (ML)

G9759.definition:
1. the surface of a body, the skin; the body  itself, (Iliad by Homer) 
2. the superficial appearance  of a thing, its colour , (Aeschulus Tragicus), etc.:—;especially the colour of the skin, the complexion , (Aeschulus Tragicus) (ML)

G9762.definition:
1. one who melts gold , of one who gilds the horns  of a victim, (Odyssey by Homer) 
2. a goldsmith , (Demosthenes Orator) (ML)

G9765.definition:
1. poured, shed , αἷμα χυτόν blood shed , (Aeschulus Tragicus) 
2. of dry things, shot out, heaped up , χυτὴ γαῖα a mound of  earth, a sepulchral mound, (Homer):—;as Substantive, χυτός, οῦ, = χῶμα, a mound, bank, dike , (Herdotus Historicus) 
3. melted , ἀρτήματα λίθινα χυτά pendants of melted  stone, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. generally, liquid, flowing , [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

G9766.definition:
1. an earthen pot, a pot for boiling, pipkin , Lat. olla, (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. χύτραι, pots of pulse  offered to inferior deities, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9768.definition: a pot with feet , or a portable stove  for putting a pot upon, (Hesiod) (ML)

G9770.definition: to be  or go lame , (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9771.definition:
1. earth thrown up, a bank, mound , thrown up against the walls of cities to take them, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dike  to hinder a river from overflowing, (Herdotus Historicus):—; a dam , (Herdotus Historicus):—; a mole  or pier , carried out into the sea, Lat. moles, (Herdotus Historicus) 
2. like Lat. tumulus, a sepulchral mound, [Refs 5th c.BC, variant datesTragica Adespota 
 
 (ML)

G9779.definition:
1. to cast into a mould (  χόανος), (Aristophanes Comicus) 
2. to cast metal: —;Pass., κεχωνευμένος (Plutarch) (ML)

G9782.definition:
1. a pair of scissors , Lat. forfex, [variant datesAnthology Palantina 
2. a building with a pointed stone roof, a vault , Lat. fornix, (Sophocles Tragicus) 
 
Deriv. unknown. (ML)

G9785.gloss: to sing along with stringed instruments
G9785.definition: to sing along with stringed instruments

G9787.definition: like a starling , i. e. speckled, dappled , ψ. ἵππος a dapple-gray  horse, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9789.definition: to falter in speech, speak inarticulately :—;so in Mid., (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

G9793.definition: a proposition carried by vote : especially a measure passed in the  ἐκκλησία, a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); τὸ Μεγαρέων ψ. the decree  concerning them, (Thucydides); so, περὶ Μεγαρέων ψ. (Thucydides); ψ. γράφειν to bring in a decree , (Aristophanes Comicus); ψ. ἐπιψηφίζειν, of the πρόεδροι, to put it  to the vote, (Aeschines Orator); ψ. νικᾶν to carry it , (Aeschines Orator); ψ. καθαιρεῖν to rescind it , Lat. abrogare, (Thucydides) (ML)

G9794.definition: to whisper, say into the ear , (Plato Philosophus):—;metaphorically, ὅταν πλάτανος πτελέᾳ ψιθυρίζῃ when the plane whispers  to the elm, (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

G9795.definition:
1. bare , 
2. of land, ψιλὴ ἄροσις a bare  corn-field, (Iliad by Homer); πεδίον μέγα τε καὶ ψιλόν (Herdotus Historicus): with genitive, γῆ ψιλὴ δενδρέων land bare  of trees, (Herdotus Historicus):—; ψιλὴ γεωργία the tillage of land for corn , opposite to γ. πεφυτευμένη (for vines  and olives) , (Aristotle Philosopher) 
3. of animals, stript of hair  or feathers, bare, smooth , δέρμα (Odyssey by Homer); ἶβις ψιλὴ κεφαλήν bald  on the head, (Herdotus Historicus) 
4. generally, bare, uncovered , ψιλὸν ὡς ὁρᾷ νέκυν (Sophocles Tragicus):—;with genitive bare of, separated from , ψιλὴ σώματος οὖσα [ ἡ ψυχή] (Plato Philosophus) b. bare, stript of appendages , ψιλὴ τρόπις the bare  keel with the planks torn from it, (Odyssey by Homer); ψ. θρίδαξ a lettuce with the side-leaves pulled off , (Herdotus Historicus); ψ. μάχαιραι swords without other arms , (Xenophon Historicus) 
5. οἱ ψιλοί (i.e. τῶν ὅπλων); soldiers without heavy armour, light troops , such as archers and slingers, opposite to ὁπλῖται, (Herdotus Historicus), etc.; τὸ ψιλόν, opposite to τὸ ὁπλιτικόν, (Xenophon Historicus); ψ. ἔχων τὴν κεφαλήν bare-headed, without helmet , (Xenophon Historicus)
